newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends flat, gilts steady in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends flat, gilts steady in dull trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday at 7.5-8.0 percent in range-bound trade, little changed from the day's opening quotes, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trades were between 7.5 percent and 8.0 percent.
"Call money rates have been drifting down gently over the past few days," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Rates opened around 9.5 percent on Monday and have gently eased since then."
He said rates were likely to ease further in the coming days to around 6.0 percent.
"At the moment it looks like rates are being held high mainly by lender quotes," another dealer said. "We should see them drop further soon."
Prices of government securities were largely steady in moderate trade, dealers said.
They said traders were cautious and unwilling to take up fresh positions unless call money fell to lower levels.

"Most of the traders built up positions in April when call money was below 1.0 percent," said a dealer. "At the moment they are only switching between stocks. Volumes should pick up if call goes down further."
Most of the day's trade was in securities with maturities up to 2002, he said.

The 13.40 percent 1999 government of India stock traded on Thursday at 104.4 rupees against Wednesday's 104.55, the 13.70 percent 1999 rose to 104.90 from 104.85 while the 12.69 percent 2002 was marginally down at 100.22 from 100.25.
Among treasury bills, the bill maturing in January 1998 yielded 9.3 percent against its last 9.25 perecnt and the April 1998 bills yielded 9.4 percent against 9.35.
